question.text: Currents of a 10 ampere and 2 ampere are passed through two parallel thin wires $A$ and $B$ respectively in opposite directions. Wire $A$ is infinitely long and the length of the wire $B$ is $2 \mathrm{~m}$. The force acting on the conductor $B$, which is situated at $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ distance from $A$ will be

solution.text:
Force acting on conductor $B$ due to conductor $A$ is given by relation $F=\frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2 l}{2 \pi r}$
$l$-length of conductor $B$
$r$-distance between two conductors
$$
\therefore F=\frac{4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10 \times 2 \times 2}{2 \times \pi \times 0.1}=8 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~N}
$$
